A fire broke out in a residential area in Baseco Compound, Port Area, Manila before noon on Saturday.

The fire in Gasangan started at 11:25 AM, according to the Manila City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) Department.

The Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) quickly raised the second alarm at 11:26 AM, then the third alarm at 11:34 AM as the fire quickly spread.

data.raw_text:
🌀 Western Pacific Tropical Bulletin 
— TYPHOON #Jangmi (DomengPH)
Issued: Saturday May 30, 2026, 4: 00 PM Philippine Time
Areas of Concern: Philippines, Taiwan, and 
the Ryukyu Islands of Japan (especially Okinawa)

Jangmi, known in the Philippines as “#Domeng,” continues to strengthen over the Philippine Sea and is now a TYPHOON tracking  northward toward the southern Japanese islands during the June 1–2, 2026, timeframe. Forecast guidance increasingly suggests the system could pass near or just west of Okinawa and portions of the Ryukyu Island chain before curving northeastward. 

🇵🇭 Philippines
Although the core of Jangmi is expected to remain east of Luzon, the cyclone is already enhancing the southwest monsoon (Habagat) which may bring periods of heavy rainfall, gusty winds, and rough seas to western sections of Luzon and the Visayas through the weekend. Coastal communities and fishermen should closely monitor local advisories due to increasing wave heights and the potential for localized flooding. PAGASA and Philippine civil defense agencies have already upgraded alerts as the system intensifies. 

🇹🇼 Taiwan
Taiwan is not currently expected to receive a direct landfall from Jangmi, but significant peripheral effects are possible between May 31 and June 2. Forecasters indicate strong winds, dangerous surf, and high waves affecting eastern, southeastern, and northern coastal waters, as well as the Taiwan Strait. Maritime conditions are expected to deteriorate considerably, and residents along exposed coastlines should remain alert for hazardous seas and squally weather bands. 

🇯🇵 Ryukyu Islands / Okinawa
The Ryukyu Islands of Japan appear to be the area facing the greatest potential impact from Jangmi. Current JTWC-style forecast guidance indicates closest approach near Okinawa around late June 1, 2026 into June 2, 2026, likely as a Category 2 equivalent TYPHOON with strong winds, torrential rainfall, dangerous surf, and possible coastal flooding. U.S. military installations on Okinawa have already entered elevated tropical readiness conditions as confidence increases in impacts across the island chain. 

Residents across Okinawa and neighboring islands should prepare for:
Damaging tropical-storm-force to typhoon-force winds
Flash flooding and landslides in mountainous terrain
Dangerous marine conditions and very rough surf
Possible transportation disruptions and power outages
Forecast models currently suggest the storm may begin recurving northeastward after passing near the Ryukyus, but even a small track shift could significantly alter impacts across Okinawa, Amami, and adjacent islands. 

🌀 SUMMARY:
Jangmi is becoming a significant early-season TYPHOON threat for the Ryukyu Islands of Japan while also generating hazardous marine and monsoonal conditions for Taiwan and the Philippines. Interests across Okinawa and the broader Ryukyu chain should closely monitor official updates from JTWC, JMA, and the Hurricane/Typhoon/Cyclone Updates & Information page.

Respectfully,

Roshin
